method: Goods trade (EUR bn, current prices) of each economy with Russia and Ukraine, 2019-2025 annual plus Jan-Aug 2026. Source hierarchy per country/flow/year: (1) reported = the economy's own customs report in UN Comtrade (public preview API, HS TOTAL, C00); (2) mirror = the partner's own report (Russia's 2019-2021 Comtrade report; Ukraine's 2019-2024 Comtrade report and Ukraine's 2025/2026 data via IMF IMTS with UKR as reporter = SSSU data), divided by the empirical median mirror/reported ratio for that flow (CIF/FOB, origin vs consignment) from 2019-2021 (RUS) or 2019-2024 (UKR) pairs; (3) imf = IMF IMTS (api.imf.org, dataflow IMF.STA:IMTS, vintage published 2026-10-01; includes IMF staff imputations for non-reporters), spliced to the Comtrade level by the median ratio over overlapping years; IMF values whose implied growth from the nearest reported year lies outside the 5-95th percentile of reporting countries' growth are rejected and replaced by (4) but kept inside the range; (4) estimated = geometric interpolation between neighbouring known years, else nearest known year x median growth of reporting countries (>USD 50m) for that flow and year pair, range from 5th/95th percentile of that growth; special cases: Belarus (official turnover statements), Uzbekistan 2025 (national statistics), Russia-Ukraine bilateral 2022+ (Ukraine's own report only). Margins (~90%): reported = +-max(3%, half the country's median |log mirror gap| 2019-21), capped 25%, default half of the flow's global median gap; range widened toward the IMF value when IMF differs (max x1.5). mirror = +-max(10%, flow median gap, country gap) capped 60%. imf = +-max(15%, mirror margin, splice factor) (x2, min 40%, for IMF staff estimates). 2026 = Jan-Aug 2026 (8 months, not annualized; '2026_annualized' gives a full-year equivalent). EU27: Eurostat Comext DS-045409 monthly Jan-Aug 2026 (EUR), spliced to the Comtrade 2025 level. Others: IMF IMTS monthly Jan-Jun 2026 x the same series' Jan-Aug/Jan-Jun 2025 ratio, spliced to the 2025 annual value; margin adds the 90th pct extrapolation error from back-testing on 2025. No monthly data: 2025 x 8/12 x median Jan-Aug 2026/2025 growth of measured countries, range from its 5th-95th percentile. 'baseline' gives the 2021 central value, the 2019-2021 average and the linear 2019-2021 trend extrapolated to 2022 as alternatives for the pre-war level.

fx.source: ECB SDW EXR.A.USD.EUR.SP00.A annual averages (USD per EUR), verified 2026-10-17; 2026 = mean of EXR.M Jan-Aug 2026
fx.note: Task-supplied rates agree to 4 decimals (2026 task value 1.1625 vs Jan-Aug mean 1.1628). Monthly IMF values converted with ECB monthly rates.

notes: Values are EUR bn. Each year: {low, central, high, basis, src}. basis in reported|mirror|imf|estimated. Self-flows (Russia with Russia, Ukraine with Ukraine) are omitted.

Empirical mirror ratios (partner report / own report, median of pairs >USD 5m): imports_from_RUS 0.847 (n=392, median |log gap| 0.35, p90 1.36); exports_to_RUS 1.320 (n=306, median |log gap| 0.28, p90 1.28); imports_from_UKR 0.810 (n=680, median |log gap| 0.20, p90 0.76); exports_to_UKR 1.388 (n=524, median |log gap| 0.41, p90 1.33). Partner-reported imports exceed own-reported exports by ~32-39% (CIF/FOB plus country-of-origin attribution, e.g. Russia/Ukraine record EU-routed Asian goods by origin), and partner-reported exports are ~15-19% below own-reported imports.

Jan-Aug 2026 growth vs Jan-Aug 2025 among measured countries (median, 5-95th pct): imports_from_RUS 0.97 (0.30-1.94, n=132); exports_to_RUS 0.95 (0.51-1.47, n=92); imports_from_UKR 0.99 (0.41-1.90, n=124); exports_to_UKR 1.05 (0.25-1.91, n=99)

Jul-Aug extrapolation back-test (predict Jan-Aug 2025 from Jan-Jun 2025 x 2024 seasonal ratio), 90th pct |log error|: imports_from_RUS 0.22; exports_to_RUS 0.14; imports_from_UKR 0.14; exports_to_UKR 0.21

Bounding check against Russia FCS aggregates (FCS: 2022 exp 592.5/imp 255.3 revised; 2023 425.1/285.1; 2024 434.5/282.8; 2025 418.3/279.0; Jan-Jul 2026 263.4/174.2 USD bn; via Interfax, TASS, investfuture.ru): 2022: partners' imports from RUS USD 610bn vs FCS exports 592.5bn (ratio 1.03); partners' exports to RUS USD 225bn vs FCS imports 255.3bn (ratio 0.88) | 2023: partners' imports from RUS USD 462bn vs FCS exports 425.1bn (ratio 1.09); partners' exports to RUS USD 245bn vs FCS imports 285.1bn (ratio 0.86) | 2024: partners' imports from RUS USD 444bn vs FCS exports 434.5bn (ratio 1.02); partners' exports to RUS USD 239bn vs FCS imports 282.8bn (ratio 0.85) | 2025: partners' imports from RUS USD 431bn vs FCS exports 418.3bn (ratio 1.03); partners' exports to RUS USD 227bn vs FCS imports 279.0bn (ratio 0.81) | 2026 Jan-Aug: partners' imports from RUS USD 315bn vs FCS Jan-Jul exports 263.4bn x 8/7 = 301bn; partners' exports to RUS USD 166bn vs FCS Jan-Jul imports 174.2bn x 8/7 = 199bn. Partners' imports from Russia match FCS exports within 2-9% (CIF vs FOB). Partners' recorded exports to Russia cover ~80-88% of FCS imports (CIF/FOB, origin attribution, transit/parallel imports); totals were NOT rescaled to FCS - the gap is a known under-coverage of the exports_to_RUS flow (~USD 30-50bn/yr) that the high bounds only partly capture.

IMF IMTS world totals (USD bn) for reference: Ukraine exports 2021 65.8, 2025 40.3; imports 2021 70.0, 2025 81.7. Russia (IMF, partner-derived after 2021) exports 2025 442.1, imports 237.9 - IMF Russia imports are below FCS, so IMF Russia-as-reporter partner data were not used.

Belarus: Belarus' own Comtrade 2019-21 report omits energy (2021 imports from RUS USD 12.0bn vs IMF 23.7bn; exports to UKR 1.2 vs 5.4bn), so IMF IMTS is used for 2019-21. IMF 2022-25 Belarus-Russia series (exports to RUS falling to USD 9.8bn in 2025) contradicts Belarusian official statements: goods turnover USD 54.7bn in 2025 (+37% vs 2021), positive Belarusian balance with Russia in 2022-25 (neg.by), goods+services USD 57.6bn 2024 (Belarus Economy Ministry via Interfax) and USD 62bn 2025 (D. Krutoi), turnover +~20% in H1 2026 (PM Turchin, rg.ru). 2022-26 Belarus-Russia flows are statement-constrained estimates with wide ranges.

Uzbekistan: IMF IMTS 2023+ values are ~3.5x Uzbek national data and Comtrade (e.g. 2025 imports from RUS USD 26.4bn vs ~8.5bn) and were excluded; 2025 from Uzbek national statistics as reported by TASS/kun.uz (Jan-Sep 2025 turnover USD 9.391bn, exports to RUS 3.245bn; full-year turnover ~USD 13.0bn per Uzbek government, 11.5bn per Russian Deputy PM Manturov - range covers both). Uzbek-Russian trade +37% y/y in Jan 2026; 2026 by rule.

UAE exports to Russia 2024-25: UAE no longer reports to Comtrade; IMF staff estimate (USD ~0.06bn) is implausible after reported 2023 EUR 4.15bn and was replaced by a growth-ratio estimate; low bound keeps the IMF value (range EUR 0.05-8bn).

Russia-Ukraine bilateral 2022+: only Ukraine's own report used (IMF Russia-as-reporter bilateral series shows ~USD 4.5bn Russian imports from Ukraine 2022-25, inconsistent with Ukraine's report of ~USD 0.02bn in 2024). 2023 Ukraine exports to Russia interpolated.

Hong Kong imports from Russia: reported EUR 11.6bn 2025 and IMF monthly imply ~EUR 18bn Jan-Aug 2026 (sharp rise from March 2026); reported data, composition not checked (likely precious metals/gold).
Taiwan (TWN): no IMF series; 2025-26 estimated by growth ratios from 2024 Comtrade ("Other Asia, nes").

Not done / limitations: Ukrstat (ukrstat.gov.ua) TLS certificate expired and Russia FCS site unreachable from this environment - Ukraine 2025/2026 by country taken from IMF IMTS (UKR as reporter, = SSSU data), FCS aggregates from press reports. China customs Jul-Aug 2026 not fetched (IMF monthly to Jun 2026 + seasonal extrapolation). Vietnam/Iran/Mongolia/Tajikistan/Turkmenistan/Algeria/Syria 2024+ come from IMF (often partner-derived) or growth estimates.

65 IMF values rejected as outliers (list in trade_full-notes.md); 40 country-flows with no data in any source set to 0 with a small upper bound (10th pct of 2021 values of all economies) - mostly tiny territories.

Use: map baseline central = 2021 central; alternatives baseline.avg_2019_2021 and baseline.trend_2022. Change vs pre-war = year value - baseline; for 2026 compare 2026 (8 months) with 8/12 of baseline, or 2026_annualized with baseline.
